subject: counting number of lineages in a region at any given time point in the tree

messages.author: e6ac6506bddc9816
messages.subject: counting number of lineages in a region at any given time point in the tree
parts:
Hi Nick,

Happy Holidays! I have a question about processing BSM output that I am struggling to figure out:

For my study I am following the approach of Xing and Ree 2017 (https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.1616063114) who used LAGRANGE to calculate a rolling speciation rate for each region for 1 myr time bins along their tree(s). The per-capita speciation rate for a focal region for each 1 myr time bin was calculated as the number of in-situ speciation events occuring in that time bin divided by the number of lineages occuring in the region in the previous 1 myr time bin. 

I have the numerator figured out using BioGeoBEARS and BSM. That wasn't hard because I could get the states reconstructed at each node (I used ML_marginal_prob_each_state_at_branch_top_AT_node in the results object for each map individually) and I know the age of each node so I could assign to a time bin.

The denominator is giving me trouble. The "number of lineages in a region" implies the number of branches reconstructed within the focal region at the cut-off of the previous bin. So for example, if I draw a line through my tree at 5 mya I would want to count all the branches currently in region A at that moment, so I can use that number to calculate the speciation rate in region A for the following time bin at 4 myr. The fact that we're dealing with branches and not nodes gives me trouble. For example, if there was an extirpation event where A was lost along a branch, I don't want to count that branch in the total number of lineages for A for the relevant time bin; however, it matters exactly where along that branch the extirpation event occurred if the branch is longer than the length of each time bin.

Do you have a recommendation for how I may do this using BSM output? Specifically, I want to count the number of branches currently in a given region at any given time point in the tree. 

Thank you for your help as always,
Best,
Liz

messages.subject: Re: counting number of lineages in a region at any given time point in the tree
parts:
Hi!  I think someone, or several people, have done this -- Julia Dupin
maybe?
(Or, maybe I did it and forgot!)

Basically you have to iterate through the BSM tables, and for each time
point, count the total number of branches, and then for each branch
existing at that time point, figure out what its range is, then tabulate.

If you don't find something obvious already published on this, we can
discuss further, it shouldn't be too hard.

Cheers!
Nick
